purpose: Demonstrate that the shared CloudEvents, evidence, provenance, permission and verification kernel works for a second institutional document surface pair.

activities.label: validate the second surface pair through the shared CloudEvents kernel
attack source identity provenance destination permission preconditions and safety
record second-surface reuse and remaining API unknowns

queries.expression: does the second surface pair use the same envelope kernel while changing only domain adapter fields
does replay across three delivery permutations preserve the same canonical event order
are synthetic document claims still tied to source entity references and independently verified
does a Nextcloud proposal remain dry-run and blocked by missing permission or stale source state

assumptions: All OpenEMR records are synthetic and contain no clinical human data.
The shared CloudEvents kernel is the only envelope validator for this surface pair.
Nextcloud is represented as a dry-run destination with explicit write permission.
Independent verification reads the synthetic source snapshot rather than trusting representation claims.
A second surface pair is evidence of structural reuse, not production interoperability.
kill_tests: Missing required input event blocks the adapter.
Mismatched source surface blocks the adapter.
Missing claim provenance blocks the adapter.
External document write blocks the adapter.
Missing destination write permission blocks the adapter.
Stale source precondition blocks the action.
Changed source snapshot is refuted by independent verification.
Enabling human data policy blocks the fixture.
unknowns: Whether OpenEMR and Nextcloud production APIs expose this exact event and folder model.
Which authentication, signing and schema registry mechanisms a live institution requires.
Whether clinical workflows need extra domain authority beyond the shared evidence kernel.
Whether a third, non-document surface pair will require new core abstractions.
